source.name: Fybertech 4chan Archive
source.short-desc: Fybertech has one of the largest collections of 2008-2014 4chan threads, outside of the fallen Chanarchive and the modern 4archive
source.capture: 638 thread pages named <board>_<threadno>.html across 29 boards (2008-2014; /co/ 227, /v/ 147, /tg/ 68 lead), plus 23 index.cgi listing pages that hold no posts. The crawl ships the rendered site tree at www.fybertech.com/4thread/ alongside the WARCs, so no WARC parsing is needed. THREE markup generations are mixed together: 420 pages in the classic template (replies in td.reply, OP loose at body level, some pages wrapping the date in span.posttime and some leaving it a bare text node, and some omitting <body> entirely), 197 in a later div.post template, and 20 that are 4chan's OWN markup and belong to chan-html instead. co_68816611.html is a fybertech error page with no posts. Timestamps are displayed New-York wall time; pages before ~2013 show no seconds, so those are minute-precision.

prepare.name: unpack the crawl if only the .7z is present
prepare.run: mkdir -p extracted && if [ ! -d extracted/www.fybertech.com ] && [ ! -d extracted/2015-02-16-WARC ]; then 7z x -aos -o./extracted source/fybertech/fybertech-2015-02-16.7z; fi

prepare.name: stage the rendered thread pages (no WARC parsing: the crawl ships them)
prepare.run: rm -rf out && if [ -d extracted/www.fybertech.com/4thread ]; then (cp -al extracted/www.fybertech.com/4thread out 2>/dev/null || cp -a extracted/www.fybertech.com/4thread out); else echo 'no 4thread/ tree; falling back to the WARCs' >&2; mkdir -p out; fi

prepare.name: assert the crawl tree actually staged
prepare.run: ls out/*.html >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'no pages in out/: extracted/www.fybertech.com/4thread is missing.' >&2; echo 'The item also ships the raw WARCs; stage those instead with' >&2; echo '  node packages/cli/src/cli.ts warc-extract --remote <host> \\' >&2; echo '    --warc "<dir>/extracted" --out "<dir>/out"' >&2; exit 1; }

prepare.name: parse the rendered pages into out-ndjson/<board>/posts.ndjson
